title: The Ramayana
objective: After this level you can retell the Ramayana of Rama, Sita and Hanuman and explain how it spread across South and Southeast Asia.
summary: Valmiki's Ramayana: Rama is exiled, Ravana carries off Sita, and Hanuman helps rescue her. The story spread across Southeast Asia, from Thailand's Ramakien to Java's temples.

cards.headline: A prince loses his throne and his wife. A monkey helps him win.
cards.body: That's the Ramayana, the Sanskrit epic of the poet Valmiki: about 24,000 couplets in seven books. And it didn't stay at home. First the story, then where it went.

cards.headline: Fourteen years in the forest
cards.body: Rama is heir to the throne of Ayodhya, but he is sent into exile for 14 years, with his wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana. Rama embodies dharma (duty, honor and loyalty): the ideal son, husband and, in the end, king. Then, in the forest, Ravana, the 10-headed demon king of Lanka, carries Sita off.

cards.headline: Hanuman to the rescue
cards.body: With the help of Hanuman, a devoted monkey general, Rama defeats Ravana and rescues Sita: a classic tale of good triumphing over evil. In India the story is still acted out. Ramlila ("Rama's play") stages it during the nine-day festival of Navratri, and Diwali marks Rama's return home from exile.

cards.headline: The story that traveled
cards.body: The Ramayana spread in many forms through Southeast Asia, especially to Cambodia, Indonesia and Thailand. Thailand's version is the Ramakien, and khon, Thailand's traditional dance-drama, is based on it. Scenes from the Ramayana are carved on Indonesian monuments, such as Panataran in eastern Java. One epic, many accents.
